title: Document Record
description: One record per document in the archive. This is the stable intermediate format described in CLAUDE.md §5. Everything downstream — search index, static site, hosted search service — is generated from these records, which is what keeps the architecture decision reversible.

id.description: Stable identifier. Derived deterministically from source_site + original_url (or S3 key when there is no URL) so re-running ingestion produces the same ID. See pipeline/records.py:stable_id.

title.description: Human-readable title. From the document itself where possible; fall back to a cleaned filename and set title_inferred.

title_inferred.description: True when the title was derived from a filename or heuristic rather than read from the document.

body_text.description: Extracted plain text, never raw HTML. Absent text means extraction failed; see extraction.status.

source_site.description: Site id; matches the site_id field in config/buckets.json.

content_type.description: Normalized content class, not the raw MIME type. mime_type carries the specific value.

publication_date.description: Date the material was published, as an ISO 8601 date or year-month or year. Null when unknown — never guess. Provenance is a first-class feature (CLAUDE.md §4).

publication_date_source.description: How the publication date was determined. Matters because much of this corpus has no reliable date.

capture_date.description: When we captured or ingested this copy. Always known.

provenance.description: Where this came from. Every search result must be able to show this.

original_url.description: The URL this document lived at on its source site. Null for objects found only in S3 with no recoverable URL.

s3_key.description: Key of the preserved original. The original is always kept; the derived text is never the only copy (CLAUDE.md §5).

file_sha256.description: Checksum of the original bytes. Distinct from text_sha256, which is used for dedup.

retrieved_from.description: Which acquisition path produced this copy.

text_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the normalized extracted text. Deduplication key — the same PDF is likely archived under several filenames across sites, so we dedup on content, not filename (CLAUDE.md §5).

duplicate_of.description: When this record shares text_sha256 with an earlier record, the id of the one we treat as canonical. Duplicates are kept, not deleted — they carry distinct provenance.

extraction.description: How the text was obtained and how much to trust it.

topics.description: Optional subject tags. Left empty until there is a reason to have them — do not invent a taxonomy before Phase 1.
